import numpy as np
centroids = np.array([[0,0], [10,10]])
point = np.array([1,1])
distances = np.linalg.norm(point - centroids, axis=1)
label = np.argmin(distances)
print(label)
questions.explanation: Distance to centroid 0 = √2 ≈ 1.41, to centroid 1 = √162 ≈ 12.73. The nearest is centroid 0, so label = 0.

from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
import numpy as np
X = np.array([[1,2],[3,4],[5,6]])
pca = PCA(n_components=2)
pca.fit(X)
print(f"{pca.explained_variance_ratio_[0]:.3f}")
questions.explanation: The data lies on a perfect line (1,2)→(3,4)→(5,6). The first principal component captures 100% of the variance.
